layout.title: How a gas stove works

shows.does: gas runs up the pipe and is lit into a flame under a pot
the open pipe roars a tall yellow flame that never stops
a knob appears on the pipe and the hand turns it down
the lazy yellow flame sends black soot up and blackens the pot's bottom
a burner tube grows over the nozzle, air streams in its holes and the flame turns blue
the thin blue flame heats one red-hot spot on the pot's bottom
a burner head caps the tube and spreads a ring of blue flames
a ring traced round the burner head
a draft blows the ring of flames out and raw gas leaks up into the kitchen
a sensor appears in the flame, its valve rod shuts and the leaking gas stops
the hand turns the knob again but the burner stays dark with the gas shut
a spark igniter clicks beside the head and the ring of flames lights
the hand turns the knob, blue flames heat the pot and it boils
the gas stove with its blue flames under the boiling pot

layout.why: A gas stove stands cut open in a kitchen; the gas is followed from the pipe through the knob, the burner tube and the head to the flame under a pot, and a hand on the knob comes back at each human step. The camera opens close on the pipe and the pot, then frames each added part and goes close where the pot scorches and the spark clicks.

sentences.text: If you light gas from a pipe under a pot, you have a stove.
But the gas never stops, and the flame roars.
So you add a knob to turn it down.
But now the lazy yellow flame coats the pot in soot.
So a burner tube mixes air into the gas.
But the tube's blue flame scorches one spot.
So a burner head spreads it into a ring.
But a draft blows the ring out, and gas leaks.
So a sensor shuts the gas when the flame dies.
But now lighting it takes a match.
So a spark igniter clicks it alight.
Turn the knob, and blue flames heat your pot.
Congratulations, you built a gas stove.

ideas.idea: lighting gas from a pipe under a pot is already a stove
the gas never stops, the flame roars all day
a knob on a valve turns the gas down
gas burning without air is a lazy yellow flame that blackens the pot
a burner tube pulls air in through its holes, so the gas burns blue
the tube's one thin flame burns one spot
a burner head spreads the flame into a ring
a draft blows the ring out and raw gas leaks
a flame sensor shuts the gas when the flame dies
with the gas shut, relighting needs a match
a spark igniter clicks it alight
turn the knob and the blue ring heats the pot
